Claim: Data-oriented modelling: architecture follows measured data structure
Evidence boundary: Repeatedly retained across real tasks; simple statistical models were kept when added channels or neural layers did not clear frozen gates.

Claim: Traditional statistics are components, not merely baselines
Evidence boundary: EXP011–015 and later real tasks repeatedly showed that statistical modelling, calibration and routing can carry most or all usable signal.

Claim: Statistical MoE routing can outperform neural routing in the tested coarse evidence setting
Evidence boundary: EXP015: availability+density OOF statistical routing outperformed the neural-routed committee across the tested availability regimes.

Claim: A shared coordination mechanism can exist and carry functional load
Evidence boundary: EXP001–010 established coordinated shared states, recurrent use, lesion sensitivity, temporal semantics and precision residual separation under controlled or limited real-measurement settings.

Claim: Shared Ganglion is the best default for new real tasks
Evidence boundary: EXP017–089 did not produce a complete, independently qualified real-task gain over appropriate statistical comparators.

Claim: The tested shared model was too small
Evidence boundary: EXP057–058 did not justify 32D/64D or longer training; these results do not diagnose insufficient capacity.

Claim: Prospective historical drug-translation prediction is established
Evidence boundary: EXP020–024 did not produce a qualified indication-specific dated terminal chronology.
The mechanism remains valid and reusable; the current engineering decision is dormancy until new evidence can change the choice.
